title: Introduce onboard sanity prober and changelog preview
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding new model versions produces a lot of manual churn: metadata shape mismatches, missing performance hints, and noisy release notes drafts. This PR adds two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight onboard sanity prober that runs as a step in the model onboarding pipeline to catch common metadata and profile regressions early, and (2) a changelog preview generator that synthesizes a human-readable draft changelog from profile deltas and metadata diffs so reviewers get a concise summary during review.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds an extensible onboard prober CLI (+ Kubernetes job runner config) that validates required metadata fields, schema conformance, and a small set of performance smoke tests (token-per-second baseline and memory footprint check) against the model profile in CI; implements a changelog preview service that consumes the profile-diff artifact and emits a compact natural-language draft suitable for quick review and copy-paste into release notes.

Key behaviors and guards: The prober is intentionally conservative — failures are informational by default and only block onboarding runs when the 'strict' flag is enabled (used by security/enterprise pipelines). Performance smoke tests run on a single small-batch local quantized variant to avoid cost. The changelog preview applies heuristics to highlight meaningful deltas (>=10% latency change, quantization-affordance changes, or added/removed capability tags) and collapses trivial metadata noise.

Checklist: - [x] add prober CLI + unit tests for metadata validation - [x] add Kubernetes Job manifest + RBAC notes for Private deployments - [x] add changelog preview generation + templating and sample outputs - [x] wire prober into onboarding pipeline as an optional step - [x] document config flags and 'strict' gating behavior - [x] add lightweight perf smoke tests and a mock runtime for CI

Commits summary: 1) introduce onboard prober CLI and validation rules 2) add perf smoke test harness and example profiles 3) implement changelog preview generator and templates 4) pipeline wiring and docs 5) tests and e2e runbook update.

Files touched (high level): - cmd/onboard-prober/main.go (CLI entrypoint, flags) - internal/onboard/prober/validator.go (schema & field checks) - internal/onboard/prober/smoke_test.go (small runtime harness) - tools/changelog/previewer.py (diff->text logic, templates) - infra/k8s/templates/onboard-prober-job.yaml (Job + RBAC snippets) - docs/onboarding/sanity-prober.md (usage and configuration) - pipeline/onboard-stages.yaml (optional step wiring)

CI & runtime notes: First CI run showed a flaky integration test in smoke_test.go on macOS runners; flaky assertion was tightened and retried. Final CI state: all checks passed (unit, lint, smoke). A single e2e run against the mock runtime was included to avoid dependence on GPU infra in CI.

Review conversation (condensed): - Liam: "Can the prober handle partial metadata (legacy uploads)?" — Answer: yes, prober supports permissive mode and emits a per-field suggestion list; added tests covering legacy cases. - Zoe: "Changelog output needs to avoid vendor/model names exposure in drafts." — Answer: previewer now redacts sensitive identifiers by default and provides a redact=false flag for internal users; documented the behavior. - Ravi: "Does the smoke test add significant CI cost?" — Answer: No, the harness runs quantized mini-inference on CPU in <30s; added a mock runtime path to bypass heavy ops for most CI runs.

Migration and rollout plan: The onboard prober is feature-flagged. We'll enable 'informational' mode by default for two weeks, collect telemetry on common failures (via telemetry events added in prober), then enable strict gating for teams that opt-in. Changelog preview will be surfaced in the onboarding UI as a draft and also stored as a companion artifact in the model release bundle.

Security & compliance: RBAC manifest includes minimal service account permissions to read model artifacts and write artifacts to the release bucket. The previewer redacts names and identifiers unless explicitly enabled; audit logs are emitted when the redact flag is turned off.

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of only generating diffs or only linting metadata, this PR provides an end-to-end lightweight probe that couples schema/quality checks with minimal runtime smoke tests and a readable changelog preview — enabling reviewers to assess impact faster and reduce onboarding back-and-forth.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main. Post-merge tasks: update onboarding runbooks (done), schedule a short internal demo for Platform and Solutions teams (scheduled), add telemetry dashboard for prober failures (follow-up ticket).

review_comments: Liam: Can the prober handle partial metadata? — Yes, permissive mode added and covered by tests.
Zoe: Ensure changelog preview redacts vendor/model identifiers by default. — Redaction added; redact=false opt-in.
Ravi: Impact on CI cost? — Mock runtime and quantized CPU path keeps runs <30s, added opt-out for heavy tests.
release_notes: Adds an optional onboard sanity prober (CLI + Kubernetes job) that validates metadata shapes and runs lightweight perf smoke tests, plus a changelog preview generator that synthesizes human-readable release drafts from profile deltas. Feature-flagged; redact defaults enabled for security.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flag rollout; add telemetry dashboard for prober failures (ENG-4681). K8s Job manifest requires access to model artifact bucket; follow RBAC manifest instructions in docs.
